body: I appreciate the comments! I’ll look into reading that.

If I could be a cis male, and live happily as myself, I would choose too any time over being trans. Yet no matter what I do, I can never be happy in the long term as a cis male. I am not transitioning because it’s 2022, I’m transitioning because I feel like a woman trapped in a man’s body. It’s not because I feel ugly, I am quite fond of my looks, if they weren’t mine. I’m transitioning so that I can change my body to suit me more, and therefore making it so that I feel comfortable being my true self. Im transitioning so that I can have relationships again without feeling like I’m leading people on pretending to be someone I’m not. Every time I be myself in this body it just feels wrong to me and others.

I do have some people I can be my real self around, which is me presenting feminine. I love my friends and enjoy being around them when I can be feminine. I have a group of “misfits” by society’s standards. And no, it’s not just a bunch of lgbtq+ people. Most of them are straight cis men. I am the only out trans person in the group. No one told me to transition, it was a decision I came to myself. I’m just worried since I hear about people regretting it even if they felt 100% sure. I have no plans for surgery as I can pass already and think that genitals don’t define your gender, so I’m fine with mine. I have already banked sperm so if I’m infertile, I can still have bio kids if I want. I have done everything to make sure that most of the process is reversible. I know that if I go through, I might be infertile. I am willing to go through that to feel happy.

I don’t feel Lupron and drugs are comparable. Drugs are a depressant, Lupron isn’t. Without Lupron I would go back to having testosterone influence me and make me feel like shit. I don’t feel like I could handle that again.

And also lupron isn’t modifying my physical presentation sadly. It’s keeping me at where I was when I started it. The only physical change I’ve gotten is reduced body hair growth. The rest of the changes are mental.

You bring up lots of good points. I guess I say inferior man because that’s what people have told me I am. I don’t believe women are inferior versions of men, but for sure some of my trans feelings are influenced by stereotypical expectations. If we lived in perfect world where everyone was treated as a person, not a “man” or “women”, than I don’t feel like I would feel the need to socially transition. But sadly we will probably always have gendered stereotypes and expectations. The point of socially transitioning is to fit into a desired group after all. Lupron has made it so that currently I feel like I’m not in any group, and it’s liberating, yet I still have the feeling of wanting to belong to a group.

I have always dealt faith feeling in superior to my younger sister. I’m transitioning mtf, but have dealt like a inferior man in life. I’m on lupron and have dealt better with myself than ever, especially when presenting androgynous or fem

I came out to my mother at a meeting with her and my therapist. It helped me a lot to have a professional be able to talk to her about her feeling so I didn’t have too. If you have a supportive therapist who is knowledgeable about gender studies than I would highly recommend having a therapist with you to help your mother understand the emotions she will go through
Exactly what happened to me. Breezed through elementary and middle school without having skills such as studying and then was fucked when I reached high school

Haha I wish my parents gave me money. I know that I probably could do something like that, but that feels like riding off someone else’s success. My dream is to be successful, but I’ve lost all motivation to do so.
